title: Claude AI Workshop Quiz
description: Prompting, Projects, Web Search, Skills, Artifacts, Connectors and MCP — scenario-based, medium level.

questions.text: A student has uploaded syllabus PDFs, class notes, and previous-year papers and wants all related conversations to remain organized in one place. Which Claude feature fits best?
questions.explanation: A Project keeps files, instructions and related chats together in one place.

questions.text: Every time you give Claude Java code, you want it to explain line-by-line, mention common mistakes, and finish with a practice question. You don't want to repeat these instructions. What should you create?
questions.explanation: A Skill packages reusable instructions that Claude applies whenever the task comes up.

questions.text: You ask Claude to create an interactive placement dashboard with buttons, progress tracking, and editable content. Which feature is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Artifacts are for standalone, interactive content such as apps and dashboards.

questions.text: You ask: "What are the latest AI hiring trends this month?" Which Claude capability is most important for this task?
questions.explanation: Recent, changing information needs live Web Search.

questions.text: Your resume is already stored in Google Drive and you want Claude to access it through an available supported integration. What should you use?
questions.explanation: Connectors let Claude access data in apps like Google Drive.

questions.text: Which statement best describes MCP?
options: A feature used only for generating presentations
A standard way for AI applications to connect with tools and data sources
questions.explanation: MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard for connecting AI apps to tools and data.

questions.text: You first show Claude two examples of professionally written emails, then ask it to write a similar email to your HOD. Which prompting style are you using?
questions.explanation: Giving examples before the task is Few-Shot prompting.

questions.text: You prompt: "Act as a senior college student and help me create a realistic routine balancing classes, study, friends, and free time." Which prompting technique is this?
questions.explanation: "Act as…" assigns Claude a role — Role Prompting.

questions.text: In the ACT prompting approach, which part controls whether Claude should respond formally, casually, humorously, or professionally?
questions.explanation: ACT = Action, Context, Tone. Tone sets the style of the response.

questions.text: You have separate Claude Projects for DBMS, Java, and Placement Preparation. You want the same "beginner-friendly explanation style" available across multiple tasks. What is the better solution?
questions.explanation: A Skill can be reused across Projects and tasks; Project instructions stay inside one Project.

questions.text: Why would you set custom instructions inside a Claude Project?
options: To define how Claude should behave specifically for that Project
To connect Claude to the internet
To automatically create an MCP server
questions.explanation: Project instructions shape Claude's behaviour for every chat in that Project.

questions.text: Claude provides an answer using live web information with source links. What should you do before using that information in an assignment?
options: Convert it into an Artifact first
questions.explanation: Citations are there so you can check the original sources.

questions.text: When connecting Claude to an external service, what is the safest approach?
options: Share your password directly in the chat
Grant only the permissions needed for the task
Store login credentials inside a Skill
questions.explanation: Least privilege: grant only what the task needs.

questions.text: Which file normally contains the main instructions for a Claude Skill?
questions.explanation: SKILL.md holds the skill's name, description and instructions.

questions.text: Why might a student create separate Projects for "DBMS Notes" and "Placement Prep"?
options: To keep their files, instructions, and conversations organized around separate goals
questions.explanation: Separate Projects keep context focused on each goal.

questions.text: You want Claude to read your resume from Google Drive and then create an interactive resume-review report. Which combination makes the most sense?
questions.explanation: The Connector reads the resume; the Artifact presents the interactive report.

questions.text: Your Project contains your own placement notes, but you also want Claude to compare them with the latest industry hiring trends. What is the best approach?
options: Delete the Project and use Web Search
Use Project context together with Web Search
questions.explanation: Combine your own Project context with fresh information from Web Search.

questions.text: Why is MCP sometimes compared to "USB-C for AI"?
options: It is a physical cable for AI systems
It provides a common standard for connecting AI applications with different tools and data sources
questions.explanation: Like USB-C, MCP is one common connector standard that works across many tools.

questions.text: You simply ask Claude: "Explain the difference between RAM and ROM in simple words." You don't need files, external apps, or reusable instructions. What is the simplest choice?
questions.explanation: A simple one-off question needs nothing more than a normal chat.

questions.text: Workflow challenge: A student wants to keep placement notes and resume files organized, reuse the same interview-evaluation rules, access a resume stored in a connected app, and create an interactive interview scorecard. Which workflow is the best fit?
questions.explanation: Project (organize) → Skill (reusable rules) → Connector (resume) → Artifact (scorecard).
